title: Oxaloacetate Restores HIF-1alpha-Mediated Mitochondrial Homeostasis to Counter Tubulointerstitial Injury in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
authors: Zhang, Yao; Ji, Jia-Ling; Yao, Dan-Dan; Zhou, Yan; Liu, Cong-Cong; Tang, Zhen-Lin; Xue, Jia-Le; Liu, Bi-Cheng; Li, Zuo-Lin; Ma, Rui-Xia
one_liner_zh: 该文研究糖尿病肾病中草酰乙酸通过PHD2/HIF-1α轴恢复线粒体稳态，虽涉及分子对接但核心为代谢与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Renal tubular injury, one of the most critical events in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), plays a pivotal role in the progression of the disease. Metabolic reprogramming of renal tubular cells emerges as a prominent pathological feature, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We established a streptozotocin-induced mouse model of diabetes. Metabolomic analysis was then used to characterise DKD-specific metabolic alterations. To test the functional consequence of a metabolic intervention, DKD mice received intraperitoneal injections of oxaloacetate (OAA). Furthermore, molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assays were used to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying OAA's effects on renal tubular injury, which were further validated in HK-2 cells exposed to high glucose. Finally, a specific pharmacological inhibitor was applied to study the relevant signalling pathway. RESULTS: Metabolomic profiling identified a marked decrease in OAA, a key tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle intermediate, in injured renal tubular cells. OAA supplementation significantly attenuated tubulointerstitial injury, as evidenced by reduced tubular cell damage, fibrosis, and macrophage infiltration. Moreover, restored mitochondrial homeostasis was observed in DKD mice after OAA treatment. Mechanistically, we found that OAA inhibited prolyl hydroxylase domain 2 (PHD2), an essential regulator of hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha), thereby stabilising mitochondrial homeostasis. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of HIF-1alpha abolished the protective effects of OAA, confirming the involvement of the PHD2/HIF-1alpha axis. CONCLUSIONS: OAA ameliorates renal tubulointerstitial injury in DKD by restoring mitochondrial homeostasis through the PHD2/HIF-1alpha axis.
abstract_zh: 背景：肾小管损伤是糖尿病肾病（DKD）中最关键的事件之一，在疾病进展中发挥核心作用。肾小管细胞的代谢重编程成为突出的病理特征，但其潜在分子机制尚未完全阐明。方法：我们建立了链脲佐菌素诱导的糖尿病小鼠模型。随后使用代谢组学分析来表征DKD特异性的代谢改变。为测试代谢干预的功能后果，DKD小鼠接受草酰乙酸（OAA）腹腔注射。此外，使用分子对接和细胞热位移实验来阐明OAA对肾小管损伤作用的分子机制，并在高糖暴露的HK-2细胞中进一步验证。最后，应用特异性药理学抑制剂来研究相关信号通路。结果：代谢组学分析鉴定出受损肾小管细胞中OAA（一种关键的三羧酸（TCA）循环中间体）显著减少。OAA补充显著减轻了肾小管间质损伤，表现为肾小管细胞损伤、纤维化和巨噬细胞浸润减少。此外，在OAA处理后，DKD小鼠中观察到线粒体稳态恢复。机制上，我们发现OAA抑制脯氨酰羟化酶结构域2（PHD2），这是缺氧诱导因子-1α（HIF-1α）的关键调节因子，从而稳定线粒体稳态。此外，药理学抑制HIF-1α消除了OAA的保护作用，证实了PHD2/HIF-1α轴的参与。结论：OAA通过PHD2/HIF-1α轴恢复线粒体稳态，从而改善DKD中的肾小管间质损伤。
